name: TinyAGI
vibe_summary: A multi-agent, multi-team orchestrator (formerly TinyClaw) aimed at running a 'one person company' of AI agents with isolated workspaces. Ships with a polished web portal (TinyOffice), team chat rooms, and Linear-style task management, but is still flagged experimental.
best_for: Solo founders wanting a team of collaborating AI agents
Users who want a polished web dashboard for agent management
avoid_if: You need a stable, production-hardened system (marked experimental)
You want a lightweight single-agent assistant
You avoid Node.js daemon/Docker operational overhead
openclaw_advantages: Native multi-team orchestration with agent hand-offs and fan-out
Built-in web portal (TinyOffice) with task/project management
Multi-provider support (Claude, Codex, custom endpoints) with token management
SQLite-backed queue with retries and dead-letter handling
openclaw_disadvantages: Experimental stability flag versus OpenClaw's more mature core
Heavier Node.js runtime and daemon footprint
Smaller ecosystem and fewer community skills/integrations
Docker runs as root, weakening in-container isolation

overview_markdown:
TinyAGI (formerly TinyClaw) is a TypeScript-based multi-agent orchestrator positioned as an 'agent teams' platform for the one-person company. It runs multiple isolated AI agents with specialized roles that collaborate via chain execution and fan-out, coordinated through a SQLite-backed message queue with atomic transactions, retry logic, and dead-letter management. It supports Anthropic Claude, OpenAI Codex, and any OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible endpoint, with per-provider API key management built in.

Its standout differentiator is TinyOffice, a browser-based control plane featuring a pixel-office visualization of agents, persistent team chat rooms, Linear-style task and project management with comments, and unified services/providers/logs tabs. Agents connect to Discord, WhatsApp, and Telegram, and a plugin system allows custom message hooks and event listeners. Installation is a one-line curl script that auto-configures and launches the daemon.

Compared to OpenClaw, TinyAGI leans harder into multi-team collaboration and dashboard UX rather than single-assistant depth. However, it self-labels as experimental, and recent commits show rapid UI churn plus some security trade-offs (e.g., Docker running as root, relying on gVisor for isolation). It's best suited for early adopters who want an agent 'company' metaphor with a rich management UI.
